promptCards.title: Moon Muffin Market Stall Details
promptCards.teacherSetup: Place this card at a description station and ask students to add three market details before drafting.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a moonlit muffin stall where your character notices one detail that helps the whole market run smoothly.
promptCards.shareMove: Invite students to read only their strongest setting detail to a partner.
promptCards.extension: Have students circle one vague word and replace it with a more exact market detail.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing includes at least three concrete setting details tied to the market scene.

promptCards.title: Puddle Planet Delivery Choice
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to pick one delivery decision and explain why the character chooses it.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a post office on Puddle Planet where your character must choose the fairest way to sort a mixed-up stack of cheerful notes.
writingLines: One reason for this choice is ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to name the choice they heard and one reason that made sense.
promptCards.extension: Add a thought bubble that shows what the character considers before deciding.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing names a clear character choice and gives a reason connected to the scene.

promptCards.title: Buttonwood Library Train Sequence
promptCards.teacherSetup: Have students number the four writing lines before they draft so the events stay in order.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write the order of events as a tiny library train carries book carts to the right reading rooms.
promptCards.shareMove: Have students swap cards and point to the word that shows each step in order.
promptCards.extension: Add one transition word to each line without changing the order.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing uses a clear beginning, middle steps, and ending in logical order.

promptCards.title: Cloudberry Clocktower Polite Dialogue
promptCards.teacherSetup: Model one line of polite dialogue, then have students write two speakers with different jobs.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a short conversation at Cloudberry Clocktower where two helpers calmly decide how to reset the snack-time chimes.
promptCards.shareMove: Let pairs read the dialogue quietly, each taking one speaker's line.
promptCards.extension: Revise one line so it sounds more like the speaker's job.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The dialogue includes at least two speakers and moves the clocktower problem forward.

promptCards.title: Tiny Lantern Reef Revision Dive
promptCards.teacherSetup: Give students a first sentence to improve and ask them to revise for clarity rather than length.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Revise a reef scene so readers can understand how the tiny lanterns guide a friendly sea parade.
writingLines: I can make it clearer by adding ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask students to share the one word or detail they changed, not the whole draft.
promptCards.extension: Use a colored pencil to underline the added revision detail.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student identifies a specific change and improves clarity in the revised sentence.

promptCards.title: Pencil Dragon Academy Sense Notes
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to use at least two senses before writing the academy scene.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a Pencil Dragon Academy lesson where careful sense details help a student remember the next writing step.
promptCards.shareMove: Invite students to trade cards and star one sensory detail they can picture clearly.
promptCards.extension: Add one more sense detail to the line that feels thinnest.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing uses two or more sensory details that fit the academy setting.

promptCards.title: Margin Note Market Problem Fix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Have students state the market problem in one sentence before choosing a calm solution.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write about a market in the margins of a notebook where tiny notes get out of order and your character finds a fair fix.
promptCards.shareMove: Ask volunteers to read only the problem and solution lines as a quick pair check.
promptCards.extension: Draw a before-and-after margin note to show how the fix changes the market.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing connects a specific problem to a specific solution that fits the notebook market.

promptCards.title: Pocket Park Notice Board Ending
promptCards.teacherSetup: Ask students to draft two possible endings and choose the one that best matches the park notice.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write an ending for a pocket park story where the final notice helps everyone understand the shared plan.
promptCards.shareMove: Let students hold up one or two fingers to show which ending they chose before explaining.
promptCards.extension: Add a final sentence that shows how the park feels after the notice is read.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The chosen ending matches the earlier story problem and explains why it fits.

promptCards.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Sentence Mix
promptCards.teacherSetup: Display short, medium, and question sentence examples before students draft the greenhouse note.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a greenhouse gear note using different kinds of sentences so the garden helpers can follow the plan.
writingLines: A longer sentence with a detail: ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Ask partners to tap once for a short sentence and twice for a longer sentence.
promptCards.extension: Revise one sentence beginning so not every line starts the same way.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The writing includes varied sentence lengths or types that remain clear.

promptCards.title: Solar Oven Picnic Station Share Card
promptCards.teacherSetup: Set a two-minute partner share and remind students to respond with one noticed detail and one question.
promptCards.studentPrompt: Write a picnic station scene you can share with a partner, showing how the solar oven team prepares a fair test snack.
writingLines: A detail I want my partner to notice is ________________________________
A question I can ask my partner is ________________________________
promptCards.shareMove: Partners give one quiet compliment about a clear detail and ask one curious question.
promptCards.extension: Add a peer suggestion box where the writer can choose one idea to try next.
promptCards.rubricLookFor: The student prepares a shareable scene and includes a specific detail for peer response.
